Package neqsim.process.equipment.reactor

Class IronSulfideWallInventory

java.lang.Object
neqsim.process.equipment.reactor.IronSulfideWallInventory
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable
public class IronSulfideWallInventory extends Object implements Serializable
Stateful inventory of iron-bearing corrosion products on a pipe or equipment wall.

The inventory separates material that is attached to the wall from material in a process stream. This distinction is important for old pipelines: iron sulfide can have accumulated during an earlier wet or sour period and can later react when oxygen is introduced during a purge, shutdown, or restart. A conventional steady-state fluid flash has no memory of that history.

ironOxideEquivalentMassKg is reported on an Fe2O3-equivalent basis. Real corrosion products can be mixtures of FeO, Fe3O4, FeOOH, and Fe2O3. The equivalent basis preserves the iron inventory without claiming a unique oxide mineral.

1.0

    • setMassesFromMeasuredScaleThickness

      public void setMassesFromMeasuredScaleThickness(double thicknessM, double skeletalDensityKgPerM3, double feSMassFraction, double feCO3MassFraction, double ironOxideMassFraction)
      Set all three inventories from a measured mixed-scale thickness and laboratory mass fractions.

      The supplied density is the skeletal (non-pore) density of the mixed corrosion product. Porosity is applied by the inventory, so do not supply an already porosity-corrected bulk density. This method is useful when an inspection reports one average scale thickness and XRD/SEM-EDS provides approximate FeS, FeCO3, and iron-oxide fractions.

      Parameters:
      thicknessM - average total scale thickness in m
      skeletalDensityKgPerM3 - non-pore mixed-scale density in kg/m3
      feSMassFraction - FeS mass fraction from 0 to 1
      feCO3MassFraction - FeCO3 mass fraction from 0 to 1
      ironOxideMassFraction - iron-oxide-equivalent mass fraction from 0 to 1
